title: Sell Mineral Rights in Bethany, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Bethany, WV | Brooke County
metaDescription: Bethany, WV mineral owner with a rural Brooke County farm tract? We buy inherited mineral and royalty interests directly, title-checked before any offer.
heroLead: Bethany is a small, rural college town in Brooke County, and the farmland surrounding it holds mineral rights that have mostly passed down through family estates rather than through active sales.
intro: Away from the river industry that shaped towns like Follansbee and Benwood, Bethany's mineral history runs quieter, mostly farmland tracts leased over the decades as operators worked north and west into Brooke County's share of the Marcellus and Utica play. Ownership here tends to still sit with descendants of the original farm family.

We buy mineral and royalty interests around Bethany directly. Because so many of these interests came through inheritance rather than a purchase, we spend real time confirming the chain of title before making an offer.

sections.heading: Farmland tracts, generational ownership
paragraphs: Bethany-area mineral tracts are frequently still held in the names of the family that farmed the surface, sometimes going back to grandparents or great-grandparents. That means title tracing often runs through a will, or through West Virginia's intestate succession rules if no will was probated.

sections.heading: Leasing reached Bethany later than the river towns
paragraphs: Operators typically worked the Ohio River corridor first before pushing leasing further into rural Brooke County. If your Bethany tract was leased more recently, the terms are more likely to already reflect a standard royalty rather than an old flat-rate structure, though we still check every lease individually.

sections.heading: Confirming heirs before we make an offer
paragraphs: When a mineral interest passed through an estate without formal probate, several family members may technically hold undivided shares even if only one person has been managing the paperwork. We identify who actually holds record title before pricing the interest, so the offer reflects real ownership.

This matters more in Bethany than in a town with a single, recently-updated tract, because rural Brooke County farms were often owned jointly by spouses and passed informally to children without anyone filing new paperwork at the courthouse. A buyer who skips that step ends up offering on the wrong percentage.

faqs.question: My grandparents owned the mineral rights but never left a will. Can I still sell?
faqs.answer: Often yes. We can work with heirship established through West Virginia's intestate succession rules, though a probated estate does make the process faster.

faqs.question: Is my Bethany tract leased at a standard royalty or a flat rate?
faqs.answer: It depends on when the lease was signed. We review the actual recorded lease to confirm the royalty structure before making an offer.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests that aren't currently under lease?
faqs.answer: Yes, unleased mineral interests are still purchasable, though the offer reflects the absence of current production.

faqs.question: How long does it take to confirm heirship on a Bethany tract?
faqs.answer: It depends on how many generations the interest has passed through. A single-generation transfer with a probated will can be confirmed quickly; multiple unprobated generations take longer to document.
